conviction_note: The company's own H1 guide (OP 2,550m) implies June-August OP of only 346m, against 628m a year ago, which already carried a 515m seasonal Takahashi Shoten returns loss, while the rest of the business grew Q1 OP 32%; an H1 beat of roughly 10-25% looks very likely and gives the company room to raise the full year again toward the IFIS 5,663m ordinary consensus. But the beat is arithmetic anyone can do from the July short, this company held its full-year plan at all three previous H1 prints, the stock fell after 7 of its last 11 prints on real release dates, and 信用倍率 is 27.7x, so p_up is only 56. The sum of the findings (+1.4) is larger than the scaled +0.6 because the findings price what the release adds and the scaled number carries the doubt about how this name reacts.
bar: Company H1 (Mar-Aug 2026) guide, revised 2026-07-09: sales 31,500m / OP 2,550m / ordinary 2,500m / net 1,600m (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708589483.pdf). There is no H1 consensus. IFIS full-year ordinary consensus is 5,663m against the company's 5,350m, unchanged over 4 weeks; the stale IFIS Q1 consensus of 1,450m was beaten by 51% (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=4763). print_vs_bar is H1 OP against 2,550m.
positioning_check: JPX short register: 0.0%, no disclosed position at or above 0.5%, unchanged (baseline, as of 2026-09-29). 信用残 on kabutan as of 10/02: margin long 102.6k shares against 3.7k short, 信用倍率 27.73x (34.13x on 09/25). The margin long is about 2.8 days of the ~37k-share daily volume and 0.45% of shares outstanding, so it is crowded in ratio terms and modest in absolute size. No option skew exists. findings.finding: The revised H1 guide implies June-August OP of 346m (2,550 - Q1 2,204), down 45% from last year's 628m. Last year's quarter included a 515m seasonal Takahashi returns loss (restated; 457m preliminary), so ex-Takahashi Q2 was ~1,144m. The ex-Takahashi business grew Q1 OP 32% (1,912m against 1,452m), with medical +29% and Creative Japan +23%. Even flat ex-Takahashi Q2 with a 600m Takahashi loss gives H1 OP ~2,750m (+8%); a 20% ex-Takahashi rise gives ~3,050m (+20%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY26 (2025-10-09) came in line with guide (OP +1.8%) and the stock moved -1.23% to the next close. H1 FY25 (2024-10-10) 'turned to a 14% decline, below plan' and the stock moved +1.72%. Q1 FY27 (2026-07-09), a 51% beat over the IFIS Q1 consensus with an upward revision and a dividend raise, moved +8.55%. Measured off Yahoo daily closes on the kabutan-listed release dates.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 86% progress rate on H1 OP is computable from the July short. What is not visible is the size of the Q2 beat. That depends on whether Takahashi's returns loss repeats at ~500m, which the company has not quantified for this year. The stock has added only ~3% since the post-Q1 close (1,448 on 07-10 to 1,497) and sits at PER 9.2 with the IFIS target at 2,365. If a 20% H1 beat were priced, the full-year consensus would be well above 5,663 and the stock would have re-rated after July.
findings.independence: Last year's H1 deck gives the Q2 segment base (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251009/140120251007569440.pdf), and last year's forecast-vs-actual notice gives the Takahashi Q2 loss (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251009/140120251009570799.pdf). These are different documents but the same company and the same arithmetic.

findings.finding: The full-year guide leaves H2 OP at 2,900m (5,450 - 2,550), +1.5% against last year's restated 2,858m, while the ex-Takahashi business is running +30%. The company broke its habit and revised up at Q1 (first upward revision in three fiscal years, passing through ~200m of a larger beat, plus 1 yen of dividend), so a second raise toward the 5,663m IFIS ordinary consensus, with a dividend bump under its 30% payout policy, is the item this release is most likely to add.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The only upward revision in the record (2026-07-09, FY OP +200m plus 1 yen of dividend) moved +8.55%. The FY guide was held at H1 in FY24, FY25 and FY26 (kabuyoho revision history), with moves of -1.23% (FY26) and +1.72% (FY25). The new-year guide on 2026-04-09 moved -4.63%.
findings.why_not_priced: IFIS consensus has sat at 5,663m for four weeks, only 6% above the company, and the stock trades at 9.2x company EPS. A market pricing a raise to ~5,800-6,000m would show a consensus revision or a re-rating after July, and neither happened. The counterweight is that the company held its FY plan at all three previous H1 prints and missed its initial FY plan in FY24 and FY25, so a hold is plausible. A hold would leave an implied H2 that looks conservative rather than a cut, which bounds the downside.
findings.independence: Revised-guide document: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708589483.pdf. Shares the H1 arithmetic with finding 1; the raise is conditional on that beat, so the two are not independent.

findings.finding: H1 net income will likely print far above the 1,600m guide because Takahashi's seasonal Q2 loss lowers group tax expense. The same mechanism put H1 FY26 net 64% above guide (2,214m against 1,350m), and Q1 net is already 1,486m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last year's +64% net beat from the same tax timing moved the stock -1.23%. The market looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: It will make a kabutan headline ('中間純利益 上振れ'), but it is a known tax-timing item that reverses in H3/H4, so it is mostly priced. It is filed small because it is below operating income with no path to the guide.
findings.independence: Q1 net of 1,486m against the 1,600m H1 guide: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708589449.pdf

findings.finding: Margin longs are crowded at 信用倍率 27.73x (102.6k long against 3.7k short as of 10/02), with no disclosed shorts to squeeze. This name has fallen after 7 of its last 11 prints on real release dates, which caps the upside reaction to a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Already partly in the baseline's priced_lean (-0.72 margin overhang), so it is sized small. It matters as a seller of strength into a beat, not as a negative on its own.
findings.independence: Baseline lean_components.margin_overhang reads the same ratio; same datum.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: plausible. H1 is likely to beat by 10-25%; the company revised up at Q1 but held at H1 in each of the last three years; the street (IFIS 5,663m ordinary) is 6% above the company. Returns: H1 dividend is 0 by policy; a year-end bump follows any net raise under the 30% payout policy; 優待 was introduced 2025-10-30 separately, not with the results. New-year guide: n/a (H1). Quarter against its own progress history: Q1 OP was 40% of FY against 29.4% last year and ~35% two years ago; H1 at 86% progress after Q1 against ~70% last year.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive against a priced lean of -0.80 that comes almost entirely from margin overhang, with a flat run-up. The strongest positive this release could carry is an FY raise plus a dividend bump, which I looked for and sized. The strongest negative is a held FY plan with the beat dismissed as Takahashi timing, as on 2025-10-09 (-1.23%). That is why p_up sits at 56 rather than 60+.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a finding resting on a 進捗率 anyone can compute from the last short is held by the price), applied symmetrically to a positive: the H1-beat finding is cut from +1.2 to +0.6 and p_up from 58 to 56
Rule 1 also cut the tax-timing net beat from +0.2 to +0.1, since last year's identical pattern was looked through
The guidance finding (+1.0) is left standing because it is the item the release ADDS
Rule 2 (negatives outnumbering positives) does not apply: one small negative; the strongest positive and negative are written in baseline_tension
